paper_metadata.title: An Empirical Study on Enhancing Explainability through Quantum Machine Learning for Credit Risk Analysis

summary: The paper evaluates a Quantum Support Vector Classifier for credit‑score classification using quantum feature maps. Classical SVC achieves ~79% test accuracy (78.7% after tuning), while QSVC with individual ZZ or Pauli feature maps reaches 75.7%, and a combined ZZPauliMap improves accuracy to 84.8% after cross‑validation and hyperparameter tuning. No hardware execution, runtime comparison, or complexity advantage is demonstrated.

experiments.description: Credit score classification using quantum feature maps (ZZFeatureMap, PauliFeatureMap, and combined ZZPauliMap) with a Quantum Support Vector Classifier, compared against classical SVC baseline.

algorithm.variant: QSVC with ZZFeatureMap, PauliFeatureMap, and combined ZZPauliMap
algorithm.convergence_criteria: stratified k-fold cross-validation and grid search for hyperparameter tuning

problem_formulation.objective_function: Credit score classification (multi-class or binary class labels not explicitly specified) using kernel-based classification in quantum feature space.

problem_instance.description: Credit score classification on a dataset with demographic and financial attributes.
